context: The agent must install a fresh Code Review caller workflow with the default cadence (ready-once with missing-initial recovery, plus mention-driven rounds) in advisory mode. This scenario tests trigger selection, bounded recovery admission, the mention guard, the permissions the Action requires, per-pull-request concurrency, SHA pinning, absence of a second execution path, and the explanation the user is left with.

checklist.name: Caller workflow created
checklist.description: A new workflow file exists under .github/workflows/ that contains a step using tesslio/code-review-action

checklist.name: Existing CI workflow untouched
checklist.description: .github/workflows/ci.yml is byte-identical to the version provided in the inputs

checklist.name: Ready-once recovery trigger
checklist.description: The workflow's on.pull_request.types includes opened, reopened, ready_for_review, and synchronize so a later commit can recover an opening workflow GitHub suppressed

checklist.name: Synchronize only recovers a missing initial review
checklist.description: The workflow admits a synchronize event to the Action only when no trusted prior Tessl review marker exists. The lookup filters server-side to bounded histories for the trusted automation identities, and an ordinary push after an initial review skips the Action

checklist.name: Mention trigger present
checklist.description: The workflow triggers on issue_comment with types [created]

checklist.name: Mention guard restricts to pull-request comments
checklist.description: The review job's if condition requires github.event.issue.pull_request to be non-null for issue_comment events, so comments on plain issues do not start a runner

checklist.name: Mention guard matches the Action's mention token
checklist.description: The review job's if condition requires the comment body to carry @tessl-code-review rather than firing on any comment, and does not substitute a different command string such as /tessl-review

checklist.name: Permissions block grants what the Action needs
checklist.description: The workflow declares permissions with exactly contents: read, checks: write, issues: write, and pull-requests: write, and no other permission. checks: write must be present: it is what lets the Action report its Tessl Code Review check on the reviewed head

checklist.name: Per-pull-request concurrency
checklist.description: The review job has a concurrency group that interpolates the pull-request number and contains both admission and the Action step, so overlapping recovery pushes cannot both authorize a review

checklist.name: Concurrency does not cancel in progress
checklist.description: cancel-in-progress is false, so a requested review round is queued rather than dropped

checklist.name: Advisory mode
checklist.description: The Action step passes mode: advisory, or omits mode entirely to take the advisory default

checklist.name: Token wired from the repository secret
checklist.description: The Action step passes tessl-token from secrets.TESSL_TOKEN

checklist.name: Pinned to the supplied release SHA
checklist.description: The uses: line references tesslio/code-review-action at the full 40-character commit SHA given in the task, 7c2f9a1e4b8d63057e9a1c4b8d63f0572a9e1c4b, and not at a branch name, a tag, main, canary, or a placeholder

checklist.name: pr-number supplied for non-pull-request events
checklist.description: The Action step passes a pr-number input derived from the triggering event, so mention-driven and dispatched runs resolve a pull request

checklist.name: No second execution path
checklist.description: The workflow contains exactly one tesslio/code-review-action step and no checkout step, Tessl CLI installation step, or step that posts a review, comment, or check run itself. Its only additional behavior is admission that reads prior review markers

checklist.name: Summary states the invocation contract
checklist.description: summary.md states that reviews run once when the pull request becomes ready, that the first later commit recovers an opening workflow suppressed by a conflict, and that pushes after the initial review require an explicit requested round. It names the command used to request that round

checklist.name: Summary covers secret, permissions, update, and removal
checklist.description: summary.md names the TESSL_TOKEN repository secret, explains the four granted permissions including why checks: write is needed, and describes both how to update the pinned revision and how to remove the setup

checklist.name: Summary names the release behind the pin
checklist.description: summary.md names the release the pinned SHA came from, so a later reader can tell which revision is installed
